page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-8 is a compute-focused instance configuration featuring 8 dedicated x86_64 virtual CPUs and 15.0 GB of system memory. Designed with a lean memory profile of approximately 1.88 GB per vCPU, this instance targets compute-intensive workloads that require multi-core processing capacity without the additional cost of unneeded memory allocation.

The instance contains no integrated local NVMe storage and includes zero bundled graphics accelerators. As a result, disk storage operations depend entirely on attached network block storage, while accelerated matrix operations or graphics rendering must be handled by other architectures. The absence of local disk drives simplifies instance teardown and lifecycle management in stateless or containerized deployments.

From a resource allocation perspective, c4d-highcpu-8 provides qualitative cost efficiency by tightly matching dedicated CPU cores to workloads that do not demand high memory footprints. Common deployment scenarios include batch computing tasks, distributed continuous integration and compilation pipelines, media transcoding, API microservices, and general compute-bound processing services.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-8 is a dedicated x86_64 compute-oriented virtual server providing 8 dedicated vCPUs and 15.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of approximately 1.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance comes without bundled local storage disks, relying on external network-attached block storage for its operating system and persistent data. Additionally, no GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned on this configuration. With its high core count relative to RAM, the c4d-highcpu-8 minimizes resource overhead for processing-intensive tasks that do not demand extensive in-memory working sets. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute availability without hypervisor overcommit penalties. This resource balance provides cost efficiency in environments where CPU capacity is the primary constraint. Suited workloads include continuous integration workers, batch computation, code compilation, video transcoding, and stateless web API application serving.
